newsitem.title: CHINA: China first half air travel up 13.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: China first half air travel up 13.7 pct.

text.p: Air travel in China rose 13.7 percent in the first six months over the same period last year, the fastest growth of all forms of public transport, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.
China recorded 25.98 million air passenger journeys in the first half, the newspaper quoted the State Statistical Information and Consultation Service Centre as saying.
Total public transport journeys increased by 1.2 percent to 2.49 billion in the same period, the newspaper said.
Rail travel slipped 14 percent to 449 million journeys, while bus travel rose 4.9 percent to 1.94 billion journeys, it said.

The centre linked the growth in air travel to a sustained rise in household incomes. A 50 percent price hike in rail tickets in October 1995 coupled with airline discounts were also likely contributors to the rise of air travel and decline in train journeys.
Total freight volume was 1.34 billion tonnes in the six-month period, up 0.1 percent from the same period last year, it said.
Rail freight rose 1.9 percent to 810 million tonnes, truck freight dropped 4.0 percent to 221 million tonnes and cargo carried by ship slipped 1.5 percent to 303 million tonnes, it said.
